indication: Prophylaxis of organ rejection in kidney, liver, and heart allogeneic transplants
regulatory_milestone: First calcineurin inhibitor; revolutionized solid organ transplantation worldwide; designated Type 1A (therapeutic gain).
notes: NDA 050573 (capsules/oral solution) and NDA 050574 (injection). Approved 1983-11-14. Sandoz merged with Ciba-Geigy in 1996 to form Novartis.

indication: Treatment of active duodenal ulcer, hypersecretory conditions (Zollinger-Ellison), and GERD
regulatory_milestone: Landmark histamine H2-receptor antagonist; became first drug in history to surpass $1B in annual global sales.
notes: Approved 1983-06-09. Glaxo merged with Wellcome (1995) and SmithKline Beecham (2000) to form GlaxoSmithKline.

indication: Treatment of lower respiratory tract, urinary tract, intra-abdominal, skin, and pelvic bacterial infections
regulatory_milestone: Third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic with broad-spectrum bactericidal activity resistant to beta-lactamases.
notes: Approved 1983-09-15. Fujisawa merged with Yamanouchi in 2005 to form Astellas Pharma.

indication: Adjunctive therapy in chronic urea-splitting urinary tract infections and prevention of struvite renal calculi
regulatory_milestone: HISTORIC FIRST APPROVAL under the Orphan Drug Act of 1983 (P.L. 97-414, enacted Jan 4, 1983); bacterial urease inhibitor.
notes: Approved 1983-05-31 under the new orphan drug provisions enacted January 1983.

indication: Treatment of serious gram-negative bacterial infections including bacteremia and septicemia
regulatory_milestone: Semi-synthetic aminoglycoside antibiotic derived from sisomicin with resistance to aminoglycoside-inactivating enzymes.
notes: Approved 1983-02-28. Schering-Plough merged with Merck & Co. in 2009.

indication: Treatment and maintenance therapy of bipolar manic-depressive disorder
regulatory_milestone: First slow-release formulation of lithium providing sustained plasma concentrations and reduced peak-related neuro/renal toxicity.
notes: Approved 1983-03-08. Ciba-Geigy merged with Sandoz in 1996 to form Novartis.

indication: Edema associated with congestive heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, and renal disease
regulatory_milestone: First standardized oral solution presentation of loop diuretic furosemide for pediatric and dysphagic clinical use.
notes: Approved 1983-11-30. Hoechst-Roussel lineage through Aventis to Sanofi.

indication: Treatment of moderate to severe hypertension
regulatory_milestone: Postganglionic sympathetic neuron blocking agent approved for stepped-care antihypertensive therapy.
notes: Approved 1982-12-29; commercially introduced spring 1983. Upjohn merged into Pharmacia & Upjohn (1995), acquired by Pfizer (2003).

indication: Adjunct to smoking cessation programs for the medical treatment of nicotine dependence
regulatory_milestone: HISTORIC FIRST FDA approval of a nicotine replacement therapy (chewing gum); marked FDA recognition of smoking cessation as a medical drug indication.
notes: Approved 1984-01-13. Marion Merrell Dow merged with Hoechst (1995), later Aventis, then Sanofi; consumer health spun off to Haleon.

indication: Treatment of hypertension and ventricular arrhythmias (premature ventricular contractions)
regulatory_milestone: Cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic antagonist with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity (ISA).
notes: Approved 1984-12-28. Wyeth acquired by Pfizer in 2009.

indication: Blockade of pharmacological effects of exogenously administered opioids in detoxified opioid-dependent individuals
regulatory_milestone: Landmark pure opioid antagonist approved under the Orphan Drug Act; announced by HHS Secretary Heckler Nov 1984; later marketed as Revia.
notes: Approved 1984-11-20. DuPont pharma unit sold to Bristol-Myers Squibb in 2001.

indication: Lower respiratory tract, acute bacterial otitis media, urinary tract, gonorrhea, and intra-abdominal infections, bacterial septicemia, and meningitis
regulatory_milestone: Gold-standard third-generation cephalosporin; high bioavailability and long elimination half-life enabled once-daily parenteral dosing.

indication: Treatment of intermittent claudication on the basis of chronic occlusive arterial disease of the limbs
regulatory_milestone: First hemorrheologic agent approved in the US; improves microcirculatory flow by decreasing blood viscosity and enhancing red cell deformability.
notes: Approved 1984-08-30. Hoechst lineage to Aventis and Sanofi.

indication: Management of hypertension, stepped-care therapy and hypertensive emergencies
regulatory_milestone: First competitive dual alpha-1 and nonselective beta-adrenergic receptor antagonist, reducing peripheral resistance without reflex tachycardia.

indication: Treatment of lower respiratory infections, otitis media, sinusitis, skin and urinary tract infections caused by beta-lactamase producing organisms
regulatory_milestone: First beta-lactamase inhibitor combination; clavulanic acid inhibits bacterial beta-lactamases, restoring amoxicillin antibacterial efficacy.
notes: Approved 1984-08-06. Beecham merged with SmithKline Beckman in 1989, later GlaxoSmithKline.

indication: Suppression of documented ventricular arrhythmias, such as sustained ventricular tachycardia
regulatory_milestone: First orally active primary amine analog of lidocaine (Class IB antiarrhythmic).

indication: Cough and upper respiratory symptoms associated with allergy or the common cold
regulatory_milestone: Standardized antitussive and antihistamine combination prescription drug product under DESI compliance.
notes: Approved 1984-01-10. Forest Laboratories acquired by Actavis/Allergan, now AbbVie.

chemical_type_description: Type 2 - New Active Ingredient / Dosage Form
indication: Relief of the inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses
notes: Approved 1984-05-31. Schering-Plough merged with Merck in 2009.
